topic: Sharp survivor-complier benefit bounds by partial transport. For finite ordered outcomes under conditional IV independence, exclusion, overlap, no defiers, positive always-selected-complier mass, and covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity with direction separated from a tie, identify the survivor-complier benefit capacity in each covariate cell; prove that the sharp endpoints of P(Y1>Y0 | S1=S0=1,D1>D0) have closed threshold min-cut formulas in both selection directions, a strongly polynomial flow algorithm, and endpoint-attaining full latent IV/selection laws; estimate the observable capacities and give face-aware directional-multiplier confidence sets for the entire identified interval. Include the three-level witness with survivor share 1/2, higher-arm mixture (0.2,0.5,0.3), lower-arm marginal (0.3,0.4,0.3), and sharp benefit interval [0,0.7], and reinterpret the Chen-Flores Job Corps wage application. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Using unnormalized cell masses ell_i=P(Y0=i,S0=1,C|x), h_j=P(Y1=j,S1=1,C|x), and m=sum_i ell_i, the presolver derived the increasing-selection lower benefit mass max(0,max_t(ell_{<=t}-h_{<=t})) and upper mass min(m,min_t(ell_{<t}+h_{>t})), with reversed-tail analogues under decreasing selection. The supplied witness gives masses 0 and 0.175, hence conditional endpoints 0 and 0.7. Direct full-LP checks matched the formulas on 100 random four-level instances in each direction; zero survivor cells, rho=1, atoms, cut ties, latent-mixture completion, and nearby mean/benefit literature were checked without a collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform validity of the estimated-active-set directional multiplier for the ratio of sums of cellwise max/min cut functionals under simultaneous cut ties, omitting zero survivor cells and using the stated margin to fix selection direction. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate small-grid rational three-level observable laws, solve the full latent-type LP in both monotonicity directions, and stop if any projected benefit endpoint differs strictly from the threshold formula.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp covariate-cell bounds on Pr(Y1>Y0 | S1=S0=1, D1>D0, X=x) under covariate-specific weak selection monotonicity in either direction when the two survivor-complier outcome submarginals are only partially transported.

source_refs.author: Xinyuan Chen, Fan Li
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.excerpt: a local table that is feasible in each covariate-dose-IV cell need not be pasteable into one full-data law

open_problems.why_unsolved: The survivor-complier literature isolates always-selected compliers but targets mean contrasts, while ordinal-benefit work optimizes a coupling after both potential-outcome marginals are available. Here those marginals are latent submeasures inside distinct IV/selection mixtures and share only an identified survivor-complier mass. Moreover, the archived lifted-transport proposal shows that locally feasible optimal tables need not generically paste into one multiple-world law. The missing proof must therefore both project the full compliance-selection polytope to two submarginals and exploit ordered threshold structure to lift every extremal flow to a single law over (Y0,Y1,S0,S1,D0,D1); ordinary Fréchet bounds or generic cellwise LP duality do neither.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp-identification theorem giving closed threshold min-cut formulas in both selection directions, a strongly polynomial flow algorithm, an explicit full-law completion at each endpoint, and the three-level (1/2, (0.2,0.5,0.3), (0.3,0.4,0.3)) construction attaining [0,0.7].

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from treatment-induced selection to failure of the usual IV estimand and then to the survivor-complier target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selection makes outcomes undefined for some units -> ordinary IV no longer answers a coherent survivor question -> principal stratification isolates survivor-compliers -> policy interest in who benefits requires a same-unit ordinal benefit region.

method_exemplars.technique: Use symbolic linear-program elimination for ordinal benefit functionals and explicit extremal joint distributions to certify sharpness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once survivor-complier submarginals are characterized, the remaining objective is the same strict-order coupling functional, but over partially transported mass.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct semiparametrically efficient orthogonal moments for weak-monotonicity selection bounds and combine them with cross-fitted nuisance estimates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The observable capacities are built from the same IV contrasts and selection probabilities; the new layer is a nonsmooth transport endpoint instead of a mean.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a uniformly valid estimated-active-cut directional-multiplier confidence set for the full survivor-complier benefit interval when several threshold cuts tie simultaneously, zero-survivor cells are omitted, and selection direction is fixed by a margin.

source_refs.author: Han Hong, Jessie Li

active-set slope estimators, multiplier critical values, and boundary-uniform confidence sets are deferred
state the candidate directional derivative or active-dual-face formula

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic max-map derivatives and naive-bootstrap failures are already covered by Fang-Santos and intersection-bound theory, a fact also recorded by the failed in-repo intersection-inference run. The unresolved object is the full composition: a random-denominator ratio whose numerator sums cellwise convex and concave cut maps, whose support changes after zero-mass cells are omitted, and whose branch direction is data-classified. Uniform validity requires a consistently estimated near-active face map and conditional Gaussian approximation along local sequences approaching multiple cut ties together; none of the cited methods proves that composition or its two-endpoint simultaneous coverage.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving both endpoint directional derivatives, consistent estimated near-active-cut sets, conditional multiplier convergence, and simultaneous confidence-set coverage uniformly over laws with arbitrary finite cut ties, positive aggregate survivor mass, and the stated direction margin.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation isolates nondifferentiability as the reason a routine plug-in bootstrap fails and makes the directional derivative the inferential object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Capacities admit root-n estimation -> tied max/min cuts create kinks -> the ordinary bootstrap targets the wrong law -> a face-aware derivative multiplier is needed for uniform interval coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the Hadamard directional derivative and apply it to a multiplier approximation of the Gaussian first-stage limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Finite maxima and minima of linear cut values have explicit directional derivatives indexed by their population active faces.

method_exemplars.technique: Localize near-binding indices and calibrate Gaussian-process suprema over an estimated contact set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneously tied threshold cuts form a finite contact set, so localization bridges population faces to feasible critical values.

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonalize numerator and denominator moments, cross-fit nuisances, and control covariate-dependent selection signs and boundary mass.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles the direction and ratio pieces; the new proof must add simultaneous nonsmoothness from several optimal cuts.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive a sharp sensitivity region for survivor-complier ordinal benefit when no-defiers and cellwise selection monotonicity are jointly relaxed by explicit compliance-defier and reverse-selection budgets.

source_refs.claim: Parameterizes IV-monotonicity violations by defier mass and complier-defier outcome-distribution differences and derives sharp robust regions.
source_refs.author: Claudia Noack

source_refs.claim: Relaxes unconditional selection monotonicity to covariate-conditional sign monotonicity but retains a definite direction within each covariate value.
source_refs.author: Vira Semenova

source_refs.claim: Provides sensitivity analysis for survivor-complier mean bounds but not same-unit ordinal benefit under monotonicity violations.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Steve Harris, Luke J. Keele
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.excerpt: both selection-helped and selection-harmed principal strata may coexist

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature separately treats compliance defiers and covariate-dependent selection signs, while the prior Lee-Gamma construction lets helped and harmed selection types coexist but targets a binary-outcome mean. Once both violations are admitted, observable IV differences are signed mixtures rather than nonnegative survivor-complier capacities. The first transport step must therefore profile latent complier/defier and helped/harmed selection masses jointly before coupling ordered outcomes, so the original threshold-cut proof and endpoint completion no longer apply.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For every stated pair of violation budgets, a finite-program or closed characterization of the sharp benefit interval with endpoint-attaining latent laws, recovery of the monotone threshold formulas at zero budgets, and a confidence region for the budget values supporting a positive lower benefit bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It turns an untestable monotonicity premise into an interpretable robust-region question with explicit sensitivity axes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Complier analysis relies on no defiers -> small violations can change latent distributions -> encode violations by transparent budgets -> determine where the survivor-complier benefit conclusion remains valid.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate defier prevalence from complier-defier distributional discrepancy, derive sharp distribution bounds at each value, and invert conclusions to form a robust region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those sensitivity parameters can be represented as additional signed capacities in the survivor-complier transport program.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate sensitivity-indexed survivor-complier components with influence functions and cross-fitting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination retains the same IV-plus-selection nuisances while replacing mean endpoints by transport endpoints.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend survivor-complier partial transport to continuous outcomes and margin-specific benefit events Pr(Y1-Y0>delta | S1=S0=1, D1>D0, X=x) with a discontinuous threshold cost.

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp Makarov-type bounds and nonstandard inference for treatment-effect distributions from identified continuous potential-outcome marginals.
source_refs.author: Yanqin Fan, Sang Soo Park

source_refs.claim: Shows that pointwise Makarov bounds need not be jointly or uniformly sharp for richer treatment-effect-distribution functionals.
source_refs.author: Sergio Firpo, Geert Ridder

source_refs.claim: Uses optimal transport and linear programming to sharply bound functionals of joint potential outcomes under instruments and additional restrictions.
source_refs.author: Thomas M. Russell

open_problems.why_unsolved: Makarov and optimal-transport results begin with complete marginal laws, whereas survivor-complier selection supplies submeasures embedded in observed mixtures. Moving beyond a finite chain removes the finite threshold network: the first proof step becomes a measure-theoretic subcoupling problem with a Hall-Strassen or Kantorovich dual, and the strict-benefit indicator is discontinuous. Existing smooth-cost transport arguments therefore do not establish dual attainment, endpoint-attaining full IV laws, or inference for this destination target.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp Kantorovich-dual or threshold characterization for both endpoints at every delta, existence of endpoint-attaining survivor-complier subcouplings and full latent completions, and a consistent estimator with a valid limit law or confidence band over a stated delta range.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates treatment-effect distributions from the limits of averages and centers sharp coupling bounds and their nonregular inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects conceal individual gains and losses -> the joint potential-outcome law is unobserved -> marginal laws still bound benefit thresholds -> survivor selection requires the same program over latent complier submeasures.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent joint-law restrictions as an optimal-transport linear program, derive a dual determining class, and certify sharpness with feasible couplings.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The continuous survivor-complier problem is an optimal subtransport problem with additional IV and selection constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Use plug-in sharp distributional bounds, derive their nonstandard asymptotic laws, and calibrate resampling for threshold endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its endpoint is the same discontinuous benefit-threshold probability once the latent submarginals are recovered.

open_problems.open_problem: Derive sharp survivor-complier benefit bounds when the ordered-outcome coupling is additionally constrained by a within-stratum Spearman or Kendall concordance band.

source_refs.excerpt: the result establishes only an outer-envelope dual representation, not sharpness or closed endpoint attainability

open_problems.why_unsolved: A concordance band adds a cross-world rank-moment constraint inside the latent survivor-complier stratum. The prior benefit-concordance run established only weak-duality outer envelopes because ordinary marginal-coupling duality did not supply the reverse inequality or endpoint attainment with the extra moment constraint. The first changed step is the threshold-cut reduction: the Ferrers transport problem becomes moment-constrained transport, and its optimizer must then be lifted through the IV/selection mixture equations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp finite-support linear-program or min-cost-flow characterization with an explicit zero-gap dual, endpoint-attaining full latent IV/selection laws, and a directional limit theorem for plug-in concordance-band endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames causal partial identification as optimization of meaningful cross-world functionals over substantively restricted couplings.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Marginal laws do not identify individual benefit -> transport bounds the joint functional -> concordance information narrows the coupling class -> impose it within the survivor-complier stratum.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt marginal-problem duality to fixed margins, a benefit-event cost, and additional moment multipliers while proving the needed closedness and no-gap step.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is precisely a transport problem with fixed submargins and a concordance moment inequality.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive directional limits and use derivative-estimated resampling when estimated endpoints switch optimal transport faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Concordance constraints create additional active dual faces, making endpoint inference nonsmooth.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Harris and Keele (2019, JASA, arXiv:1704.05706) define survivor-complier effects under selection on treatment, derive sharp mean bounds, and provide efficient ML-compatible estimation.
Chen and Flores (2015, JBES, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2014.975229) jointly handle noncompliance and employment selection and bound mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers.
Dong and Heiler (2026, arXiv:2606.09223) sharpen intensive-margin mean bounds under endogenous treatment and weak selection monotonicity and add orthogonal DML inference, but not same-unit ordinal benefit.
Lee (2009, ReStud, DOI 10.1111/j.1467-937X.2009.00536.x) supplies the foundational monotone-selection trimming construction behind the Job Corps literature.
Semenova (2025, JoE, arXiv:2008.12720) allows covariate-specific selection directions and boundary-aware orthogonal inference, but targets mean Lee regions rather than same-unit benefit.
Gabriel, Sachs and Jensen (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2305.10555) derive symbolic sharp ordinal benefit and no-harm bounds under imperfect randomization, without truncation-defined survivor strata.
Lu, Ding and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS, arXiv:1507.01542) establish probability-of-benefit estimands and sharp ordinal coupling bounds from fixed marginals.
Chen and Li (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2403.08927) identify efficient principal-stratum win-type estimands via U-statistics; their cross-unit comparison differs from same-unit benefit.
Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466609990168) establish treatment-effect-distribution bounds and document nonstandard inference.
Firpo and Ridder (2019, JoE, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2019.04.012) show pointwise Makarov bounds need not be jointly sharp for richer distributional functionals.
Russell (2021, JBES, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2019.1684300) gives an optimal-transport/linear-program framework for cross-world functionals with instruments and added restrictions.
Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763), Hong and Li (2018, JoE), and Chernozhukov, Lee and Rosen (2013, Econometrica) are the closest tools for tied max/min faces.
Noack (2026 working paper, arXiv:2106.06421) gives sharp sensitivity regions for IV defiers, but does not combine defiers, survival selection, and same-unit benefit.
Imai (2008, Statistics & Probability Letters, DOI 10.1016/j.spl.2007.05.015) proves sharp truncation-by-death bounds by contaminated-data constructions, an important full-law sharpness model.
The unoccupied intersection is finite-order same-unit benefit, latent survivor-complier submeasures, covariate-specific weak selection direction, constructive threshold-flow sharpness, and simultaneous-tie inference.
